function: Learned end-to-end modulation, beamforming and symbol detection: TX and RX diffractive metasurface stacks act as autoencoder encoder and decoder (p. 1-2).
system: Transmit and receive UPAs with stacked passive transmissive metasurface layers (D2NN/SIM), typically 4 layers of 16x16 elements per side, one RF chain, 28 GHz (p. 3, 9).
method: Complex-valued autoencoder; metasurface phases trained end to end with Wirtinger gradients and mini-batch SGD (Adam) on cross-entropy; supervised, offline, no fine-tuning or meta-learning (p. 6, 9).
data_channel: Custom simulated correlated Rician channel (LoS plus Rayleigh NLoS with sinc spatial correlation), K_R mostly 0 dB; 3200 random training samples; no standardized or measured data (p. 5, 9).
test_conditions: Trained at SNR −10 dB, K_R 0 dB; tested at −32 to 0 dB. Other runs vary training SNR, channel rank, K_R; no unseen scenario (p. 11-12).
baselines: Only non-learned: 16-QAM with maximum ratio transmission (MRT) using 81 RF chains; no earlier learned method; other curves are variants of the proposed system (p. 11).
metrics: Training cross-entropy loss and symbol error rate (SER) versus SNR, number of layers and elements, channel rank and Rician factor (p. 9-12).
complexity: Order of complexity of the diffraction computation: O(N^2) for RSF versus O(N log N + N) for FFT-based ASM; no FLOPs, parameter count or runtime reported (p. 8).
q1_support: p. 5: "correlated Rician fading channel that captures both deterministic line-of-sight (LoS) propagation and stochastic multipath". Custom simulated Rician model (Eqs. 7-12); no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data is used.
q2_support: p. 11: "trained under channel conditions with a Rician factor KR = 0 dB and an SNR of −10 dB, and tested under SNR conditions ranging from −32 dB to 0 dB". Only an SNR sweep; rank and Rician-factor runs (p. 11-12) never test a network on a condition it was not trained for.
q3_support: p. 11: "are selected as representatives of traditional modulation and beamforming methods" (16-QAM with MRT). Non-learned baseline only; no earlier learned method for the same function is compared, so the learned-baseline half is missing.
q4_support: p. 8: "direct matrix multiplication incurs a complexity of O(N 2 ). In contrast, the angular spectrum method implemented with FFT reduces the complexity" to O(N log N + N). Order of the training-time diffraction computation; no FLOPs or runtime.
q5_support: p. 9: "3200 randomly generated data samples". Self-generated simulation data; no code or data link, DOI, public dataset or measurement is given anywhere in the paper.
notes: The PDF is the arXiv v1 preprint (2506.02411) titled 'Baseband-Free End-to-End Communication System Based on Diffractive Deep Neural Network'; it prints no journal DOI, so the DOI-title match cannot be checked from the file. Area 1 chosen because the main metric is SER (p. 9, 11), although the SIM phases also act as a transmit beamformer (area 3), so the reviewer may confirm. q4 counts the stated O(N^2) to O(N log N) order of the diffraction calculation used in training (contribution list, p. 3); the deployed inference is analog and has no digital cost figure. Page 9 defines SER as correctly detected over transmitted symbols, evidently a slip. Rank and Rician-factor figures (p. 11-12) read as per-condition training; the text does not say otherwise.
